title: HubSpot vs SuiteCRM
comparison_markdown:
# HubSpot vs SuiteCRM (2026)

## Overview
HubSpot and SuiteCRM are two popular customer relationship management (CRM) tools that help businesses manage their sales, marketing, and customer service activities. This comparison is useful for businesses considering switching from HubSpot to SuiteCRM, particularly those looking for a self-hosted solution with more control over their data. The core use case for both tools is to streamline CRM processes, and the key reason someone would switch is to reduce costs or gain more control over their data.

## Key Differences
* Cost: HubSpot offers a free plan, but its paid plans can be expensive, whereas SuiteCRM is free and open-source.
* Data ownership: SuiteCRM allows users to have full control over their data, whereas HubSpot stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: HubSpot is generally easier to set up, whereas SuiteCRM requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: HubSpot is more scalable, with better support for large teams and enterprises.
* Integration with marketing automation: HubSpot has more advanced marketing automation features, whereas SuiteCRM has more limited capabilities in this area.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | HubSpot | SuiteCRM |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $15-$800+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1,200-$4,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $4,800-$16,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**HubSpot:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Advanced marketing automation features
* Good customer support
* Scalable and reliable
* Integrates well with other HubSpot tools
* Limited control over data
* Can be expensive
* Limited customization options
* Not suitable for very small teams
**SuiteCRM:**
* Free and open-source
* Self-hosted option for full data control
* Highly customizable
* Suitable for small and medium-sized businesses
* Limited marketing automation features
* Can be complex to set up
* Limited customer support

## When to Choose Each
HubSpot is a good choice for large teams and enterprises that need advanced marketing automation features and are willing to pay for them. It is also a good choice for businesses that want a easy-to-use, scalable, and reliable CRM solution. SuiteCRM, on the other hand, is a good choice for small and medium-sized businesses that want a free and customizable CRM solution with full control over their data. It is also a good choice for businesses that want a self-hosted option and are comfortable with managing their own servers.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from HubSpot in CSV format.
2. Set up a new SuiteCRM instance on your own server.
3. Use the SuiteCRM import tool to import your data from the CSV file.
4. Configure your SuiteCRM instance to match your business needs.
5. Test your SuiteCRM instance to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
SuiteCRM is a production-ready CRM solution for most users, but it may require some technical expertise to set up and customize. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that SuiteCRM's marketing automation features are not as advanced as those of HubSpot. We recommend switching to SuiteCRM if you are a small or medium-sized business that wants a free and customizable CRM solution with full control over your data, but if you are a large team or enterprise that needs advanced marketing automation features, you may want to stick with HubSpot.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 employees that do not need advanced marketing automation features
* Medium-sized businesses with fewer than 50 employees that want a self-hosted CRM solution
* Businesses that want a free and customizable CRM solution
* Businesses that want full control over their data
* Businesses that are comfortable with managing their own servers and do not need advanced customer support

## FAQ
### Is SuiteCRM free?
Yes, SuiteCRM is free and open-source.
### Can I self-host SuiteCRM?
Yes, SuiteCRM can be self-hosted on your own server.
### Does SuiteCRM have advanced marketing automation features?
No, SuiteCRM's marketing automation features are not as advanced as those of HubSpot.
### Can I export my data from HubSpot and import it into SuiteCRM?
Yes, you can export your data from HubSpot in CSV format and import it into SuiteCRM using the SuiteCRM import tool.
### Is SuiteCRM suitable for large teams and enterprises?
Not yet, SuiteCRM is more suitable for small and medium-sized businesses.

# Mailchimp vs Listmonk (2026)

## Overview
Mailchimp and Listmonk are both email marketing tools that help businesses manage their email lists and create campaigns. This comparison is useful for businesses and marketers who want to switch from a proprietary, paid solution to a self-hosted, free alternative. The core use case for both tools is email marketing automation, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Mailchimp has a free plan and paid plans starting at $13/month, while Listmonk is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: With Listmonk, users have full control over their data, while Mailchimp stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Mailchimp has a more user-friendly interface and easier setup, while Listmonk requires more technical expertise to set up and configure.
* Scalability: Listmonk can be more scalable than Mailchimp since it can be self-hosted on the user's own servers.
* Feature difference: Mailchimp has built-in e-commerce integration, while Listmonk requires third-party integrations for e-commerce functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Mailchimp | Listmonk |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $13-$350+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $30-$50/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $100-$200/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Mailchimp:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Built-in e-commerce integration
* Large user community and support resources
* Free plan available
* Limited control over data and customization options
**Listmonk:**
* Free and self-hosted
* Full control over data and customization options
* Scalable and flexible
* Open-source and community-driven
* Requires technical expertise to set up and configure
* Limited user support resources compared to Mailchimp

## When to Choose Each
Mailchimp is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses that want an easy-to-use, all-in-one email marketing solution with built-in e-commerce integration. It's also a good choice for businesses that don't have the technical expertise to set up and configure a self-hosted solution. Listmonk, on the other hand, is a good choice for larger businesses or enterprises that want full control over their data and customization options. It's also a good choice for businesses that have the technical expertise to set up and configure a self-hosted solution and want to reduce costs.

## Migration Path
1. Export your email list from Mailchimp in CSV format.
2. Set up and configure Listmonk on your own server.
3. Import your email list into Listmonk using the CSV import tool.
4. Configure your email templates and campaigns in Listmonk.
5. Test and verify that your email campaigns are working as expected.

## Our Take
Listmonk is still a relatively new and developing platform, and while it shows promise, it may not be production-ready for most users right now. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Listmonk requires a good understanding of Linux and server administration to set up and configure. However, for businesses that value control over their data and customization options, and have the technical expertise to set up and configure a self-hosted solution, Listmonk is definitely worth considering.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 employees that don't need built-in e-commerce integration
* Medium-sized businesses with 10-50 employees that want to reduce costs and have more control over their data
* Enterprises with over 100 employees that have the technical expertise to set up and configure a self-hosted solution
* Businesses that value open-source and community-driven software
* Teams with existing Linux and server administration expertise that want to self-host their email marketing solution

## FAQ

Yes, Listmonk is free and self-hosted, which means you can use it without paying any monthly fees. However, you will need to pay for your own server costs.
### Is Listmonk as easy to use as Mailchimp?
No, Listmonk requires more technical expertise to set up and configure than Mailchimp. However, once set up, it can be just as easy to use.

Yes, you can import your email list from Mailchimp into Listmonk using the CSV import tool.

No, Listmonk does not have built-in e-commerce integration like Mailchimp. However, you can integrate it with third-party e-commerce solutions.

Yes, Listmonk can be suitable for large enterprises that have the technical expertise to set up and configure a self-hosted solution and want to reduce costs.

title: WordPress.com vs Ghost

# WordPress.com vs Ghost

## Overview

Hosted blogging and website platform. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Ghost is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: WordPress.com costs Free / $4-$45+/month; Ghost is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: WordPress.com is Proprietary; Ghost is MIT
- **Data ownership**: Ghost can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Ghost eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Ghost has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | WordPress.com | Ghost |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $4-$45+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### WordPress.com

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Ghost

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [TryGhost/Ghost](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost) * ~47k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose WordPress.com if:** WordPress.com is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Ghost if:** Ghost is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from WordPress.com in its standard export format, review Ghost import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Ghost is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid WordPress.com tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Ghost instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for WordPress.com, switching to self-hosted Ghost will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on WordPress.com until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated WordPress.com paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Ghost free to use?
Yes. Ghost is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from WordPress.com to Ghost?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your WordPress.com data, follow the Ghost import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Ghost get regular updates?
Yes. Ghost has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Ghost without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Ghost development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [WordPress.com](https://wordpress.com) and [Ghost](https://ghost.org) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Ghost is a free, self-hosted alternative to WordPress.com. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.
